title.narrative: Collaboration for Complex Challenges: addressing the food-biodiversity-climate nexus

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The C3 Labs project seeks to redefine how socioeconomic benefits can be achieved by placing inclusivity at the core of its methodology. In contrast to many traditional GEF projects that prioritize solution development before fully engaging communities, this initiative integrates local voices and expertise at every stage—from identifying challenges to co-creating and implementing solutions. This approach ensures that inclusivity is not a secondary consideration but the foundation upon which the project is built. The active involvement of Indigenous peoples, women, and marginalized communities is not merely encouraged—it is essential to the project's success, driving the design, execution, and outcomes of the Collaboration Labs. By embedding this process-first approach, the C3 Labs methodology aims to generate deeper socioeconomic benefits. Locally co-designed solutions are more likely to be relevant, embraced, and sustained by the communities they aim to serve, ensuring long-term impact. The focus on cross-sector collaboration and capacity building aims to equip the Lab Fellows with skills in systems thinking and adaptive management, empowering them to address future challenges with confidence and resilience. In alignment with GEF Core Indicator 11, the project will directly benefit at least 120 participants, ensuring equitable representation and meaningful engagement. Gender equity is also central to the project’s design, with a 50/50 split between men and women anticipated in participant selection. This balance reflects the project’s commitment to diverse and inclusive participation, aligning with GEF’s strategic emphasis on gender equity. The project expects to directly engage 120 high-intensity participants, including 60 Fellows (30 each in Kenya and Thailand) and 60 participants in the Global Learning Lab. However, the potential socioeconomic benefits extend far beyond this number. Each Fellow represents key institutions or communities and is positioned to influence colleagues, stakeholders, and community members through the co-creation and implementation of systemic solutions. By conservative estimates, each Fellow’s engagement could benefit at least 10 additional individuals within their professional networks, while community-driven interventions stemming from the Labs are likely to indirectly impact hundreds more. By funding C3 Labs through the Innovations Window, the GEF supports a pioneering approach to achieving socioeconomic benefits that are equitable, inclusive, and scalable. The project bridges gaps between theory and practice, demonstrating how inclusivity not only strengthens social resilience but also ensures that solutions are tailored to local realities and needs. By integrating local voices into decision-making from the outset, the C3 Labs methodology aims to empower communities to take ownership of solutions, driving long-term, systemic improvements in livelihoods and well-being. If the methodology’s effectiveness is demonstrated in this project, this would position C3 Labs as a model for transformative development, showcasing how systems thinking and collaboration can enhance socioeconomic benefits across diverse contexts.

To test and validate a scalable Fellowship Program and Collaboration Lab methodology that can strengthen collaborative capacity, catalyze increased collaboration, and accelerate institutional reform to support more collaborative and systemic development practices.
